svg.title: DDR video recognition and Microsoft Fabric architecture
svg.desc: A local Python desktop app analyzes recorded or captured video and emits validated events. Independent paths publish live state through Fabric Rayfin and SQL Database to a React browser scoreboard, and durable event history through SQLite and Eventstream to Eventhouse and a Real-Time Dashboard. An expanded player logon flow shows organizer Microsoft sign-in, a station-specific React check-in kiosk, authenticated registration functions, SQL game and player records, a returned player pass, and the desktop registration relay. Player names enrich the live scoreboard; registration events are acknowledged only after durable local enqueue, then delivered through Eventstream to Eventhouse. Official unmodified product icons identify the products; custom app components use text labels.
svg.text: From gameplay video to live scores and event history
OpenCV: arrow and judgment shape matching
EasyOCR: score / combo digits in a worker
No video analysis in the browser
Calculates player metrics from judgment events
Node.js Rayfin SDK worker via private pipes
Latest state only; no event-replay backlog
Share live scoreboard: independent on/off control
Azure Event Hubs SDK: retry until acknowledged
Connect to Fabric: independent on/off control
History is independent of the React scoreboard: the live page does not query Eventhouse.
A second route in the same hosted React application
New registrations look up the latest game in SQL first. These are the same Rayfin, SQL and desktop services shown above.
Organizer signs in with Microsoft once.
Players do not need Microsoft accounts.
Player chooses normal or Easy mode.
Sends request UUID, station and optional special entry.
Require active / not ended + live heartbeat.
Check P1/P2 slot; lock normal/Easy mode.
Generate pass; retry UUID reuses the saved registration.
One player per game / station slot
Generated name + six-digit PIN + game GUID.
Special entries receive a name without a PIN.
This is registration, not a player sign-in credential check.
Desktop polls pending rows; acknowledges only after durable enqueue.
The same worker keeps GameSession active with a heartbeat.
Node SDK reads rows with eventQueued = false.
Python creates user.register with session + P1/P2.
Save to the same SQLite outbox as gameplay.
Next cycle: SQL eventQueued = true after local save.
Failure: leave SQL pending and retry with the same event ID.
> React scoreboard, matched by game + P1/P2.
Names only in live snapshots, never player PINs.
Share live scoreboard + Connect to Fabric must be on.
eventQueued means locally queued, not ingested.
PINs exist in SQL, the outbox and Eventhouse.
Easy mode flags future leaderboard exclusion.
Video and reference images stay local.
VS Code + Rayfin CLI deploy the app.
Original official icons: Microsoft Fabric, Python Software Foundation, React. Unmodified artwork; labels identify actual products.
Rayfin and custom components use text labels, not substitute logos. Access restrictions, mode rules and artwork sources: docs/architecture.md.
